initialized.note: handshake bookkeeping; the current handshake works without it

item/autoApprovalReview/completed.note: each auto-review already emits a guardianWarning notification, which codex.el renders as a status line with risk and authorization. This would only add structure to information already shown.

item/autoApprovalReview/started.note: the only signal of the 2.0-2.5s pause while auto-review runs (measured 2484ms, 1983ms). Real everyday traffic here, since ~/.codex/config.toml sets approvals_reviewer = auto_review. Payload captured. Needs a screen capture to know how the CLI shows the pause.

item/commandExecution/outputDelta.note: REAL BUG, not just missing polish: an interactive or never-exiting command sends item/started and deltas but no item/completed, so codex.el renders nothing at all for it (captured: an interactive python3 got 15 deltas and never completed). Params {threadId,turnId,itemId,delta}; concatenated deltas are byte-identical to the completed item's aggregatedOutput, so streaming must not double-render alongside item/completed. Needs a codex_gt.py screen capture before implementing.

item/commandExecution/terminalInteractio.note: captured {threadId,turnId,itemId,processId,stdin} -- the only protocol source of injected stdin. Belongs with item/commandExecution/outputDelta, since the owning item never completes and nothing about the session is shown today. Needs a screen capture first.

item/fileChange/outputDelta.note: the schema states it outright: 'Deprecated legacy notification for apply_patch textual output. The server no longer emits this notification.' Confirmed absent across 7 sessions, including with patch streaming events enabled.

item/fileChange/patchUpdated.note:
fires only with -c features.apply_patch_streaming_events=true, and then carries a strictly poorer diff than item/completed already renders (captured: '@@
-four
+FOUR
' versus '@@ -3,2 +3,2 @@
 THREE
-four
+FOUR
'). Zero events under default config.

item/mcpToolCall/progress.note: Codex accepts MCP progress and does not forward it. Proved with a probe MCP server: Codex sent progressToken 1 and the server logged 5 successful notifications/progress during a 5s tool call; not one reached the client.

item/permissions/requestApproval.note: FIRES, payload captured, but needs two non-default gates: -c features.request_permissions_tool=true plus approvalsReviewer 'user' (this config's auto_review silently approves it). Reply has no decision field -- you grant by returning the subset you allow, confirmed by deliberately mis-granting. CLI's TUI rendering NOT captured; codex_gt.py cannot set approvalsReviewer.

item/plan/delta.note: belongs to plan mode, which an app-server client cannot enter in 0.145.0: the only schema entry point (CollaborationMode) is referenced by no request. turn/plan/updated, already handled, covers the update_plan checklist. Zero events including with -c collaboration_mode=plan.

item/reasoning/textDelta.note: zero events across 7 sessions, including with -c show_raw_agent_reasoning=true. Raw chain-of-thought is not delivered for this ChatGPT-auth model; reasoning items arrive as {summary:[],content:[]}. item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta, already handled, is what actually streams.

item/started.note: captured TUI shows no in-progress item block: while a 14s command ran the CLI displayed only the Working status line and '1 background terminal running', rendering the item on completion as codex-app-server.el already does. No in-progress behavior to mirror.

item/tool/call.note: server->client request for a dynamic tool the CLIENT registered. DynamicToolSpec is referenced by no request in the 0.145.0 surface, so nothing codex.el can send would make this arrive.

item/tool/requestUserInput.note: implemented from the app-server schema, which is authoritative for the request and reply shapes. The CLI's own presentation was NOT captured: no configured tool asks this and no listed experimental feature enables it (checked experimentalFeature/list), so no trigger was found. Prompt wording is this client's own and has not been diffed against the CLI.

marketplace/add.note: marketplace management belongs in the CLI

marketplace/remove.note: marketplace management belongs in the CLI

marketplace/upgrade.note: marketplace management belongs in the CLI

mcpServer/elicitation/request.note: Allow and Cancel implemented against a captured request and the CLI's own prompt. The CLI also offers 'Allow for this session' and 'Always allow'; those record the choice in the response _meta, an encoding that was not captured, so they are deliberately not offered. Form-mode input is also unimplemented: every captured request had an empty requestedSchema.

mcpServer/oauth/login.note: reachable but not completable here: an unconfigured name returns -32600, and all three configured MCP servers are local stdio with no OAuth. Completing it needs a remote OAuth provider and interactive browser consent, so the {authorizationUrl} response was never observed.

mcpServer/oauthLogin/completed.note: notification half of the OAuth flow; not observed for the same reason as mcpServer/oauth/login. Shape is schema-only: {name, success, error?, threadId?}.

process/exited.note: legacy predecessor of the command/exec family. Only arrives after a client process/spawn, a method absent from the exported schema though still dispatched. Unreachable unless codex.el adopts the deprecated family.

process/outputDelta.note: same legacy process/* family as process/exited; not observed even when spawning (buffered mode). Unreachable without adopting the deprecated family.

remoteControl/status/changed.note: remote control state; agent.el reads this from the footer today

review/start.note: the CLI's /review feature has no Emacs entry point

skills/changed.note: nothing to invalidate: codex.el never caches skills, it calls skills/list with forceReload each time /skills runs. Verified to fire in response to skills/extraRoots/set.

skills/extraRoots/set.note: works with field 'extraRoots' (not 'roots') and fires skills/changed. NOT a parity gap but a real capability gap in this setup: agent-codex-skill-directories is used only by agent.el's own skill discovery, so skills in those directories are invisible to the Codex agent in an app-server session. Implementing means a codex.el option for extra roots pushed at thread start -- a new feature, so it needs a decision rather than a capture.

thread/approveGuardianDeniedAction.note: blocked: params require echoing back a GuardianAssessmentEvent, which the schema leaves untyped ('Serialized codex_protocol::protocol::GuardianAssessmentEvent'). Probing walked serde errors (missing id, then status, then a source nested in action) without reconstructing it. It can only be answered with an event codex.el received, and no guardian denial could be provoked to capture one.

thread/archived.note: emits {threadId} right after the thread/archive response. Redundant for codex.el's own /archive, which already reports from the response. Only value would be an archive performed by another client, and there is no cached thread list to refresh -- /resume re-queries thread/list every time.

thread/deleted.note: emits {threadId} after the thread/delete response; /delete already reports from the response. Same reasoning as thread/archived.

thread/environment/connected.note: cloud environments are not used from Emacs

thread/environment/disconnected.note: cloud environments are not used from Emacs

thread/goal/clear.note: goal is partly handled; cleared is, clear is not

thread/goal/get.note: captured response is {goal: null}; thread/goal/updated and thread/goal/cleared already keep the buffer in step, so a getter adds nothing.

thread/inject_items.note: programmatic injection, not a user action

thread/loaded/list.note: captured response is only {data:[threadId],nextCursor} -- ids of in-memory threads, no metadata. thread/list already backs the resume picker with full thread objects including preview.

thread/metadata/update.note: captured: params take only gitInfo (branch, originUrl, sha) -- it is for a client to report git metadata to the server, not for renaming a thread. Sending {name:...} errors with 'gitInfo must include at least one field'. No Emacs surface needs it.

thread/read.note: captured response returns the same thread object thread/list and thread/start already return (id, preview, forkedFromId, historyMode, timestamps). No surface needs a single-thread fetch.

thread/realtime/outputAudio/delta.note: voice mode; no audio path in Emacs

thread/realtime/sdp.note: voice mode; no audio path in Emacs

thread/rollback.note: schema says verbatim 'DEPRECATED: thread/rollback will be removed soon', and it only edits thread history without reverting files the agent wrote. codex.el has no undo surface; building one on a method upstream is removing would be wasted.

thread/settings/updated.note: could not trigger: thread/settings/update from this client returns {} and emits no notification, so it appears to exist for out-of-band changes (another client or remote control) that a single Emacs client will not see. Not observed here, so not implemented rather than guessed.

thread/unarchive.note: archive is handled, unarchive is not

thread/unarchived.note: emits {threadId} after the thread/unarchive response; /unarchive already reports from the response. Same reasoning as thread/archived.
